make.name: Renault
make.description: French carmaker and one of Europe's earliest volume EV makers: the Zoe (2012-2024) was Europe's best-selling EV for years, and the Kangoo Z.E. its best-selling electric van. Today's E-Tech Electric range includes the Renault 5, 4, Twingo, Megane and Scenic, plus electric Kangoo, Trafic and Master vans.

models.name: 5 E-Tech Electric
models.description: Retro-styled electric supermini inspired by the 1972 Renault 5, built at Douai, France, on the AmpR Small platform. Revealed in February 2024 and on sale from late 2024; an August 2026 update added an LFP entry version and more range.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with 40 kWh (95 or 120 hp) and 52 kWh (150 hp) batteries. From August 2026 the entry 'Five' version uses a 36.5 kWh LFP pack with 110 hp, and the other versions gained range.

models.name: 5 Turbo 3E
models.description: Limited-run (1,980 cars) high-performance electric homage to the 1980s Renault 5 Turbo, announced in March 2025 with a carbon-fibre body, rear in-wheel motors and an 800 V, 70 kWh battery. Deliveries are planned from 2027.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-wheel drive by two in-wheel motors, about 400 kW in total.

models.name: 4 E-Tech Electric
models.description: Electric small crossover reviving the Renault 4 name, built at Maubeuge, France, on the AmpR Small platform shared with the Renault 5. Sales began in March 2025 with deliveries from June 2025; an N1 van version followed in December 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with 40 kWh (120 hp) and 52 kWh (150 hp) batteries; a two-seat van with the 52 kWh battery was added in December 2025.

models.name: Twingo E-Tech Electric
models.description: Renault's A-segment city car. The third-generation Twingo got a rear-motor electric version (Twingo Electric) in 2020-2024; the fourth-generation Twingo, built at Novo Mesto, Slovenia from 2026, is electric only and priced under 20,000 euros.

generations.name: Third generation (Twingo Electric)
generations.description: Electric version of the rear-engined Twingo III: 22 kWh battery, 60 kW rear motor, AC charging only (up to 22 kW). Not sold in the UK.

generations.name: Fourth generation
generations.description: All-new electric-only Twingo on the RGEV small platform: 27.5 kWh LFP battery, 60 kW front motor, 50 kW DC charging.

models.name: Megane E-Tech Electric
models.description: Electric compact crossover-hatchback built at Douai, France, on the CMF-EV / AmpR Medium platform shared with the Nissan Ariya. On sale in Europe since February 2022; a June 2026 facelift switched to a single 67 kWh LFP battery with 165 kW DC charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch version with 40 kWh or 60 kWh NMC batteries and 96 kW or 160 kW front motors. The 40 kWh version was dropped in March 2025.

generations.name: Facelift (LFP)
generations.description: June 2026 facelift: new front end, a single 67 kWh LFP battery (up from 60 kWh NMC), DC charging up to 165 kW, 11 kW bidirectional AC with V2L, and only the 160 kW motor.

models.name: Scenic E-Tech Electric
models.description: Electric family crossover on the AmpR Medium platform, revealed in September 2023 and on sale from spring 2024; European Car of the Year 2024. In September 2026 the batteries were updated (67 kWh LFP and 89 kWh NMC).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Five-seat crossover replacing the combustion Scenic MPV. Launched with 60 kWh (125 kW) and 87 kWh (160 kW) NMC batteries; from September 2026 these became 67 kWh LFP and 89 kWh NMC.

models.name: Zoe
models.description: Renault's first purpose-built electric supermini and for years Europe's best-selling EV. Built at Flins, France, from December 2012 to March 2024 (about 427,000 cars); a 2019 facelift (Z.E. 50) added a 52 kWh battery and CCS fast charging.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original Zoe: 22 kWh battery with the Chameleon AC charger (no DC), then the 41 kWh Z.E. 40 battery from late 2016 and the 80 kW R110 motor from 2018.

generations.name: Facelift (Z.E. 50)
generations.description: Restyled front and new interior, 52 kWh battery, the 100 kW R135 motor and optional 50 kW CCS DC charging. Production ended at Flins in March 2024.

models.name: Twizy
models.description: Two-seat (tandem) electric quadricycle sold mainly in Europe. Built in Valladolid, Spain (2012-2018) and then Busan, South Korea (2019-2023); production ended in September 2023 and the Mobilize Duo replaces it.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 6.1 kWh battery; 45 km/h (4 kW) and 80 km/h (13 kW) versions, plus a one-seat Cargo.

models.name: Fluence Z.E.
models.description: Electric version of the Fluence compact sedan with a 22 kWh battery, built in Bursa, Turkey (2011-2013) and designed for Better Place battery swapping. Production then moved to Busan, where it was sold as the Renault Samsung SM3 Z.E. until 2020.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-wheel-drive sedan with a 22 kWh swappable battery behind the rear seats.

models.name: City K-ZE
models.description: Small electric hatchback based on the Kwid, built in Shiyan, China by the eGT New Energy joint venture (Dongfeng, Renault, Nissan) from 2019. Sold in Europe as the Dacia Spring and in Brazil and Latin America as the Renault Kwid E-Tech.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 26.8 kWh battery and a 33 kW motor in China; the Kwid E-Tech for Brazil (2022) has a 48 kW motor.

models.name: Kangoo E-Tech Electric
models.description: Electric version of Renault's compact van and leisure-activity vehicle. The Kangoo Z.E. (2011-2021) was Europe's best-selling electric light commercial vehicle; the third-generation Kangoo E-Tech Electric (2022-) adds a passenger version and optional 80 kW DC charging.

generations.name: Second generation (Kangoo Z.E.)
generations.description: Kangoo II van with a 22 kWh battery and 44 kW motor; the Z.E. 33 (2017) raised the battery to 33 kWh. AC charging only.

generations.name: Third generation (Kangoo E-Tech Electric)
generations.description: All-new Kangoo III: 45 kWh battery, 90 kW motor, 11 kW AC standard and 80 kW DC optional. Van from June 2022, passenger version from October 2022.

models.name: Trafic Van E-Tech Electric
models.description: Electric version of Renault's mid-size van. The Trafic III-based Trafic Van E-Tech Electric (presented 2022) uses the Master's 52 kWh battery; a new skateboard-platform, 800 V Trafic Van E-Tech electric built at Sandouville opens for orders from late 2026.

generations.name: Third generation (Trafic Van E-Tech Electric)
generations.description: Trafic III with a 90 kW motor, 52 kWh battery and optional 50 kW DC charging.

generations.name: New Trafic Van E-Tech electric (SDV platform)
generations.description: Software-defined skateboard platform with 800 V architecture, 60 or 81 kWh batteries; 81 kWh orders from late 2026, 60 kWh from early 2027.

models.name: Master E-Tech Electric
models.description: Electric version of Renault's large van. The third-generation Master Z.E. (2018) started with a 33 kWh battery and was upgraded to 52 kWh as Master E-Tech; the fourth-generation Master (2024-) offers 40 or 87 kWh batteries and 130 kW DC charging.

generations.name: Third generation (Master Z.E.)
generations.description: Master III with the 57 kW R75 motor; 33 kWh at launch, 52 kWh with 22 kW DC from late 2021.

generations.name: Fourth generation
generations.description: All-new Master presented November 2023, on sale spring 2024: 40 or 87 kWh battery, 96 kW or 105 kW motor, 300 Nm, up to 130 kW DC.

legacy_notes.note: Renault 5 E-Tech: legacy row shows an 'EPA range' of 180 mi (never EPA-rated; not sold in the US), a 50 kWh battery (actual 52 kWh), a currency-less price of 27000 and a link to the 2021 prototype page. Mapped to Comfort Range 150hp 52 kWh.
Zoe R135 marked 'available', but Zoe production ended in March 2024; 'EPA range' 180 mi is invented, and 130 kW DC charging is wrong (Zoe max 50 kW DC). carmodel_ended '2024-30--03' is malformed.
Zoe 22 kWh (2012) marked 'available' with 130 kW charging: the 22 kWh Zoe had no DC charging and ended in 2016. Mapped to Q210 22 kWh.
Zoe R110 41 kWh (Z.E. 40, 2018-2019) marked 'available'; 'EPA range' 140 mi invented. trim_first_released contains a stray newline.
Megane E-Tech EV60 220hp. 'EPA range' 217 mi invented (not sold in US). Replaced by the June 2026 facelift with a 67 kWh LFP battery; mapped to the 2022 EV60 220hp variant.
Scenic E-Tech Long Range 87 kWh: first released '2023' is the reveal; production/sales began 2024. 'EPA range' 265 mi invented. Superseded by the 89 kWh battery in September 2026.
Scenic E-Tech Comfort Range 60 kWh (170hp). Legacy row reuses full_slug 'renault-scenic-etech' of row 187 (duplicate slug). Superseded by the 67 kWh LFP Comfort Range in September 2026.

gaps: Prices: no clean list prices sourced for most current Renault versions (UK site prices include the Electric Car Grant; French configurator not readable). Only Megane 2026 (DE), Twingo Electric (launch) and City K-ZE (CN) carry prices.
Renault 4 E-Tech: ev-database lists 2026 LFP versions (37 kWh 110hp, 40 kWh 120hp, revised 52 kWh) mirroring the Renault 5 update, but no Renault source could be read to confirm; not added.
Renault 5 E-Tech 2026 update: press release confirms LFP only for the 36.5 kWh Five; whether the 40/52 kWh versions also switched to LFP is unconfirmed.
Scenic E-Tech 2026 battery update: power/torque/0-100 for the 67 kWh and 89 kWh versions not sourced; 60 kWh DC kW not reliably sourced.
Zoe 22 kWh versions: only NEDC ranges exist (210/240 km); NEDC is not an allowed cycle, so range left null.
Master Z.E. 52 kWh WLTP range conflicts (190 km en-wiki vs 244 km de-wiki); left null. Master IV power per battery and WLTP ranges not sourced.
Kangoo E-Tech: 2025-2026 changes not checked; Grand Kangoo E-Tech (7-seat) not verified.
City K-ZE: current production status in China not verified (model left 'current' because the Kwid E-Tech was still sold in Latin America; Renault Argentina withdrew it before July 2026).

Not added (outside makes or unverified): Mobilize Duo/Bento/Limo (Renault Group's Mobilize brand), first-generation Kangoo Electri'Cité (pre-2008), Zoe Van, Kangoo Z.E. Maxi, Flexis Estafette/Goelette E-Tech vans (no source read), Renault Korea EVs, E-Space and Emblème concepts.
